en.title: Mnemonic 1: Major Cosmogony Theorists
en.phrase: "G. L. H. (Georges Lemaître, George Gamow, Hubble expansion)"
en.decryption: Key figures of the expanding Big Bang model: **L**emaître proposed the 'primeval atom'; **G**amow added nucleosynthesis calculations; **H**ubble proved expansion observationally.

fact.en: Trap 1: Expansion of Matter: During cosmic expansion, space itself expands. Galaxies and stars do not grow in physical size. A common exam trap is saying that stars or planets expand.
fact.hi: Trap 1: Expansion of Matter: During cosmic expansion, space itself expands. Galaxies and stars do not grow in physical size. A common exam trap is saying that stars or planets expand.

fact.en: Trap 2: Big Bang Proposer: Georges Lemaître first proposed the theory of the expanding universe in 1927. George Gamow later developed it. Do not confuse Lemaître with Hubble (who proved it observationally) or Hoyle (who coined the name 'Big Bang' as a mockery).
fact.hi: Trap 2: Big Bang Proposer: Georges Lemaître first proposed the theory of the expanding universe in 1927. George Gamow later developed it. Do not confuse Lemaître with Hubble (who proved it observationally) or Hoyle (who coined the name 'Big Bang' as a mockery).

fact.en: Trap 3: Steady State Density: The Steady State theory does NOT say density decreases as space expands. It claims density remains constant because new matter is created out of nothing as space expands.
fact.hi: Trap 3: Steady State Density: The Steady State theory does NOT say density decreases as space expands. It claims density remains constant because new matter is created out of nothing as space expands.

fact.en: Trap 4: Nebular Hypothesis Focus: Do not confuse theories of the **Universe's development** (Big Bang, Steady State) with theories of the **Solar System's origin** (Nebular Hypothesis, Planetesimal Hypothesis).
fact.hi: Trap 4: Nebular Hypothesis Focus: Do not confuse theories of the **Universe's development** (Big Bang, Steady State) with theories of the **Solar System's origin** (Nebular Hypothesis, Planetesimal Hypothesis).
